abstract: Background: Molecular changes in peripheral tissues may provide insights into cognitive aging, but identifying relevant genes without using behavioral outcomes for feature selection remains challenging. Results: We applied tensor decomposition-based unsupervised feature extraction to publicly available hippocampal and colonic transcriptomic and promoter DNA methylation profiles from mice across five age groups. A tensor comprising tissue, molecular modality, age group, biological replicate, and gene dimensions was constructed using 16,080 shared genes. Higher-order singular value decomposition identified a component with a monotonic age pattern, shared tissue contributions, and opposing transcriptomic and methylation contributions. This component yielded 1,577 selected genes without using cognitive scores for feature selection. The corresponding colonic methylation score correlated with overall cognition (r=0.589; Benjamini--Hochberg-adjusted P=9.87 x10-7), although no significant associations remained after age adjustment. The selected genes were enriched for enteric neuronal and glial markers derived from a published single-cell atlas, with 5.10-fold and 4.65-fold enrichment, respectively. Comparison with the broadest available Boruta-selected gene set identified only 64 overlapping genes, leaving 1,513 genes selected exclusively by the tensor approach in this comparison. These remaining genes retained significant enrichment for synaptic processes and enteric neuronal and glial signatures using library-specific backgrounds. Conclusions: Unsupervised tensor integration recovered an aging-associated relationship between colonic methylation and cognition while identifying a largely distinct set of functionally coherent candidate genes. These findings complement supervised feature selection and provide candidates for investigating enteric neural involvement in cognitive aging, without establishing an age-independent association or a causal gut-to-brain mechanism.
